sources.text:
18 lip UKVI English Language Tests: Your Essential Guide to IELTS and PTE
If you’re applying for a UK visa—whether to study, work, or settle—you’ll likely need to prove your English proficiency with a Secure English Language Test (SELT). The UK Home Office only accepts SELTs from approved providers. Among the most widely accepted and trusted options are IELTS for UKVI and PTE Academic UKVI.
In this guide, we’ll walk you through both tests to help you understand which one aligns best with your visa type and language needs.
IELTS for UKVI: Widely Recognized and Trusted
IELTS for UKVI is a version of the globally recognized IELTS test that’s specifically approved for UK visa applications. It assesses all four language skills: listening, reading, writing, and speaking.
IELTS Test Options:
• IELTS for UKVI (Academic or General Training) Suitable for student visas, work visas, and other general immigration routes
• Suitable for student visas, work visas, and other general immigration routes
• IELTS Life Skills (A1, A2, B1) Designed for specific visa categories such as spouse/partner visas and citizenship/settlement applications Focuses on speaking and listening only
• Designed for specific visa categories such as spouse/partner visas and citizenship/settlement applications
• Focuses on speaking and listening only
Who It’s Best For:
• Applicants who need a well-established test accepted by a wide range of UK institutions and employers
• Those applying for visas requiring detailed assessment across all language skills
• Individuals more comfortable with a traditional exam structure and face-to-face speaking component
PTE Academic UKVI: Fast, Modern, and AI-Scored
PTE Academic UKVI is a fully computer-based English language test approved by UKVI. It uses AI-driven scoring to ensure consistency and quick turnaround times, assessing speaking, listening, reading, and writing in one session.
PTE Test Options:
• PTE Academic UKVI Suitable for student and skilled worker visas
• Suitable for student and skilled worker visas
• PTE Home (A1, A2, B1) Designed for visa categories that only require speaking and listening, such as family or settlement applications
• Designed for visa categories that only require speaking and listening, such as family or settlement applications
• Applicants looking for a fast and efficient testing process with quick results (often within 48 hours)
• Those who prefer a fully digital, integrated test experience
• Candidates comfortable with computer-based interaction for all skills, including speaking
Booking Your SELT
When booking a test for your visa, make sure to:
• Choose the UKVI-approved version of the test
• Select an official UKVI-approved test centre
Final Thoughts
Both IELTS for UKVI and PTE Academic UKVI are excellent, UKVI-approved options that serve a wide range of visa categories. Each has a unique structure and delivery style, designed to support different testing preferences and visa needs.
Choosing the right test depends on your visa type, timeline, and personal comfort with the test format. Whichever you choose, make sure it meets UKVI requirements and is taken at an approved test centre.

UK government Secure English Language Tests
From 6 April 2015, the UK government made changes to the list of qualifications it considers Secure English Language Tests (SELTs) for visa purposes. For qualifications completed on or after 6 April 2015, the following qualifications only are considered SELTs:
• IELTS taken at UK government-approved test centres (IELTS for UKVI)
• Trinity ISE taken inside the UK
• Pearson Test of English Academic (PTE Academic)
• LanguageCert International ESOL
You can find more information about the policy on the UK Visas and Immigration web pages:
Applying for a UK visa: approved English language tests
The government allows universities to accept achievement in non-SELT qualifications as evidence of English language proficiency. The University of Sheffield accepts all the qualifications listed on our English language requirements webpages, including all IELTS qualifications, for direct entry to its undergraduate and postgraduate degree courses.
English language requirements for undergraduate applicants
English language requirements for postgraduate applicants
Students applying for courses offered by the University's English Language Teaching Centre (ELTC) or the University of Sheffield International College (USIC) are advised to contact the ELTC and USIC for information about English language requirements.
Information for ELTC applicants is also available on the following web page:
Entry levels for Summer School

A global reputation
Sheffield is a world top-100 research university with a global reputation for excellence. We're a member of the Russell Group: one of the 24 leading UK universities for research and teaching.

sources.excerpt: PTE Academic test takers typically received their results within just 2 days. Find out why and what should you do if yours take longer.
sources.text:
How long will I wait for my PTE Academic results?

Most test scores are now returned within just 2 days
During 2018 students, migrants, and professionals that sat PTE Academic received their scores in even less time than ever before. In fact, during 2018, 85.7% of PTE Academic test takers received their results within just 2 days.

Why could my score take longer than 2 days?
There are a number of reasons why a score may take over 2 days. These can include:
Certainty: Our system sometimes flags results for additional review which can take more time. Because PTE Academic is used to make important decisions, it is important that we get your score right every time and this can take extra time.
Security: Before releasing a score, we need to ensure the person that took the test is who they say. Our biometric security systems identify when a test taker took the test under another name and that will trigger an investigation.

Are there tips for getting a faster score?
Your PTE Academic score will be returned as soon as we have marked it. There are a few things you can do to reduce the chance of delay:
Never create a duplicate Pearson VUE account as it will slow down the return of your results.
Make sure you read the that includes all the policies and procedures.
Follow all instructions carefully when creating your account and booking your test.
Create your account using a personal email that you check regularly so we can communicate with you directly.

I have not yet received a score. What should I do?
5 days or less since your test:
You need to wait for an email from us telling you your score is ready to be released. Alternatively, you can log into your account at any time. Learn how to access your score.
Over 5 days since your test:
If you have not received your score after 5 days since your test, and we have not contacted you, please contact us.

Are you interested in working as a nurse overseas? With the right qualifications, your passion for nursing could help you begin a new chapter in Australia, the US, or the UK.
In this guide, we’ll learn about what you’ll need to do to work as a registered nurse in each country, as well as what employment opportunities waiting for you abroad. Let’s explore:

Nursing in Australia: requirements
The UK has long drawn people from around the world to live, work and study. It boasts an excellent healthcare system and impressive universities. Its countryside and cities are dotted with historic buildings and castles. Another big plus? The UK is incredibly diverse. According to the Migration Observatory at the University of Oxford, about 14% of the UK’s population was born abroad, and 35% of immigrants live in London. And, many of the UK’s migrants come to work. In fact, in 2019 48% of EU residents moved to the UK to work, while 21% of non-EU residents did.
So what kind of jobs are there in the UK for international applicants? The UK has a skills shortage for a long list of occupations, and professionals who can fill them will have an easier time applying for a UK work visa under the new points-based immigration system.
In this blog, we’ll explore what top professions can help give you an advantage when applying for a UK work visa, and insight on how to get a job in the UK.

The top jobs in the UK for international applicants
The UK has two shortage occupation lists. One outlines occupations in healthcare and education that need more personnel. The other list features occupation shortages from a range of different fields – including the arts, science, and IT.
To be eligible for a Skilled Worker visa in the UK, you need to reach 70 immigration points. And working in a job on the Shortage Occupation List counts for 20 points – which can provide you with a big advantage. We’ll expand on a few top jobs on the list:

1. Nurses
The UK has faced a nurse shortage for a long time. Right now, England needs to fill more than 36,000 positions, making it an excellent place to look for work if you’re a nurse wanting to move abroad. Already, about 15% of nurses in the UK are trained overseas.
However, nurses and other healthcare professionals were added to the Shortage Occupation List just this March. “Every year we welcome healthcare workers from across the world to our United Kingdom, with many having played a key role on the frontline of the NHS during the recent pandemic,” said the UK Minister for Future Borders and Immigration, Kevin Foster, in a statement.
The move, he said, will help ensure international healthcare professionals get the immigration status they deserve.
Learn more about how to register as a nurse in the UK.

2. Pharmacists
Pharmacists were also added to the UK’s Shortage Occupation List in 2021. While not as in short supply as nurses, there’s a pharmacist vacancy rate of about 8% in hospitals. Again, this means there could be of opportunity for internationally-trained pharmacists to find a job in the UK.
To work as a pharmacist in the UK, you need to register with a regulatory body called the General Pharmaceutical Council, which you can learn more about on the NHS website. (The NHS is the UK’s publicly funded healthcare system).

3. Engineers
There are also plenty of engineering jobs on the shortage occupation list. From civil engineers to mechanical engineers, to electrical engineers and everyone in-between engineers from around the world are in high demand in the UK.
Depending on the field of engineering you work in, you’ll have to make 80% of the going rate for the job to be eligible for a Skilled Worker visa. That’s between about £26,160 and £29,600 per year.

4. Secondary education teachers
Secondary education teachers who teach math, physics, modern foreign languages, and computer science are some other jobs on the list. If you’re a trained teacher outside the UK, you can work without getting Qualified Teacher Status (QTS) for four years. But after that, you’ll have to become a qualified teacher in the UK.
You can learn more about teacher salaries on the UK Department of Education website. To qualify for a visa, you’ll have to earn at least £20,480 (or more depending on where you’re located).

5. Graphic designers
Are you a graphic designer? Well, you’re in luck. Graphic designers are also a sought-after profession in the UK. It’s common for graphic designers to work on a freelance basis. But keep in mind: to qualify for a Skilled Worker visa, you’ll need to get a job sponsorship in the UK from an employer.
You’ll also have to earn 80% or more of the going rate for graphic designers in the UK. This is about £18,800 per year.

How to get a UK work visa
A Skilled Worker visa lets you work in the UK with an employer who is approved by the Home Office, which is a UK government department. As we mentioned above, you’ll have to reach 70 immigration points to be eligible. Having a job offer from an employer, professional skills, and English proficiency all contribute to your points.
Depending on your situation, you may decide to apply for another type of visa or immigration route, such as the EU Settlement Scheme or UK Graduate visa. There is also a Health and Care Worker visa, which enables healthcare professions to work with the NHS.

How to find a job in the UK
So, how can you find an employer in the UK to sponsor you? There are lots of job boards that are related to specific professions. For example, the UK’s Department of Education offers a website to search for teaching vacancies by location. There’s also Nurses.co.uk, which features thousands of nursing jobs. More generally, websites like Reed and Jobsite are also good places to look for employment in the UK.
All in all, the UK is an excellent place to call home. And better yet, there’s plenty of job opportunities to help you thrive.

sources.excerpt: Confused between PTE and IELTS for UKVI? Compare both tests to find the best option for your UK visa application. Learn more with IDP Malaysia!
sources.text:
PTE or IELTS for UKVI - which should you take?
Are you planning to study, work and live in the UK? If so, you’ll have to pass your English proficiency test and two popular options come up - the IELTS for UKVI and the UKVI PTE.
While both of them are engineered for the UKVI standards, there are significant differences that you must know before making a choice.
In this article, we will go through the differences between UKVI PTE and IELTS for UKVI so that you can make an informed decision to reach your goals.

What Is UKVI PTE?
Launched in 2009, the PTE is an English language test that was launched by Pearson Inc. It has two tests: PTE Academic and PTE General, both computer-based and automated.
These tests have only begun to be accepted in recent years by governments like Australia and New Zealand for visa purposes.
PTE-takers will have to sit for the UKVI Academic test for a visa application.

What Is IELTS for UKVI?
Set as the golden standard for English proficiency tests, IELTS was launched in 1980 and evaluates the fluency of English in both written and spoken formats.
Accepted by over 13,500 institutions in more than 140 countries, IELTS is the most recognised test of its kind, and the most popular. It has both paper-based and computer-based versions of its test, which is split into four sections: speaking, writing, listening and reading.
If you lean towards reliability and decide to go with IELTS, the suitable test option would be the IELTS for UKVI Academic.

Understanding the PTE and IELTS for UKVI tests

1. Both tests allow students to study in the UK
If you want to further their studies in the UK, the UKVI Academic version of both the IELTS and PTE are accepted.
Both tests assess the four same skills and are recognised by numerous education institutions based in the UK.

2. Both tests help individuals live and work in the UK
If you are seeking a job as well or looking to live in the UK, you can also take either the IELTS for UKVI Life Skills A1 and B1 or PTE UKVI Home A1, A2 and B1.
Approved by the UK home office for visa applications, the UKVI versions of the tests are only available at test centres that meet the administrative requirements outlined by the UK Home Office.
In addition, your test report form will look slightly different than the regular PTE or IELTS tests.

3. IELTS is the preferred qualification vs PTE
As IELTS is the world’s number one English test for migration, it is still favoured over the PTE by most. This is an important distinction o be aware of.
Besides that, PTE is a much newer test as compared to the IELTS for UKVI, and is not as recognised globally.
In fact, over 13,500 organisations worldwide trust IELTS’ evaluation of English language skills while only around 3,000 organisations accept the PTE.
If you are looking for the widest breadth of acceptance from a test, IELTS will be the right choice to make. The last thing you want is for your certification to not be recognised, and still ending up needing to take the IELTS test.

4. IELTS offers the option of paper and pen test
If you’re more comfortable with using pen and paper to write your answers, then IELTS for UKVI would be a better option.
This is because the PTE is available only on computer, whereas with IELTS you will have the flexibility to choose between taking your test on computer or paper in many locations globally.
Not everyone is comfortable keying in their answers or taking a test on a computer. If that’s you, then IELTS is the way to go.

Take the next step towards studying and working in the UK
Now that you know the differences between the IELTS vs PTE tests, choosing the right one should be a breeze!
If you value widespread recognition of your test, then IELTS is hands down the choice for you.

sources.text:

Other useful tests

Visas: you need an approved SELT
For most UK visas that ask for English, the Home Office accepts only a Secure English Language Test (SELT) from an approved provider. You must take it at an approved test location, and you must receive the result within two years before you apply. As of September 2026, the approved tests are:
• IELTS SELT Consortium: IELTS for UKVI (Academic or General Training) and IELTS Life Skills.
• Pearson: PTE Academic UKVI and PTE Home.
• LanguageCert: International ESOL SELT, Academic SELT and General SELT.
• Trinity College London: ISE and GESE SELTs (in the UK).
• PSI: Skills for English UKVI (outside the UK).
When you book, choose the UKVI version. IELTS for UKVI and PTE Academic UKVI have the same content and format as the standard tests, so our IELTS and PTE Academic practice tests prepare you for them. We do not offer practice for LanguageCert, Trinity, Skills for English, PTE Home or IELTS Life Skills.

Studying at a UK university
For degree-level study on a Student visa you need English at CEFR B2. You can prove it with a SELT, but a university that is a Higher Education Provider may also assess your English itself. This is why universities can accept tests that are not SELTs, such as TOEFL iBT, the Duolingo English Test or Cambridge C1 Advanced. For study below degree level, the requirement is B1 and a SELT is normally needed. Always check your university's list.

Work visas, settlement and citizenship
• Skilled Worker: new applicants have needed B2 since 8 January 2026. People who already held the visa before that date need only B1 when they extend.
• Settlement (ILR) and citizenship: you currently need a B1 speaking and listening qualification, such as a SELT at B1 or above.
• Coming change: from 26 March 2027, the requirement for settlement on many routes, including Skilled Worker and Global Talent, rises to B2.

Nurses and midwives
The NMC accepts only IELTS Academic and OET as English tests for registration, with minimum scores in each skill. That registration requirement is separate from your visa.

Preparing for a UKVI test
IELTS for UKVI uses the same Listening, Reading, Writing and Speaking papers as IELTS Academic or General Training. PTE Academic UKVI is the same computer-based test as PTE Academic. The only differences are how you book and where you sit it: choose the UKVI option and take the test at an approved SELT centre. This means you can prepare with standard practice material. Start with a full timed test to find your weakest skill, then focus on that skill before you book. Check the CEFR level your visa route needs and the matching score for your test on GOV.UK, because different routes need different levels.

Ireland: English tests for study, work and nursing
Ireland is not part of the UK visa system, so the UK SELT rules do not apply there. Here is what Irish universities, employers and the nursing board ask for.

Study visas
Immigration Service Delivery (ISD) publishes minimum scores for students applying for a study visa. For higher education courses you need a result from a recognised provider, and the certificate must be issued within two years of your course start date. Foundation and second-level courses have a lower minimum than other courses. The list includes:
• IELTS Academic and IELTS UKVI
• TOEFL iBT
• PTE Academic
• Duolingo English Test
• Cambridge English exams
• LanguageCert, Trinity College London, Oxford Test of English, Skills for English and others
If you are coming for an English language course, you do not need a certificate from a test provider, though a visa officer may ask for other evidence. Colleges and universities also set their own scores, and these are often higher than the visa minimum. We do not offer practice for LanguageCert, Trinity, Oxford Test of English or Skills for English.
NMBI accepts only IELTS Academic (including IELTS Academic for UKVI) and OET. It does not accept IELTS One Skill Retake, IELTS Online or OET@Home. Results must be less than two years old.
Registering with NMBI is a separate process from getting an employment permit or visa, so plan for both.

Work and citizenship
Ireland does not have a UK-style list of approved tests for work permits. Employers and professional regulators decide what English you need. For citizenship, there is no English test at present. In September 2026 the government announced plans for a longer residence period and a language and civics requirement. These are proposals and not yet law, so check the ISD website before you apply.
Until any change becomes law, citizenship applications are decided under the current rules.

Choosing and timing your test
The ISD list is broad, but your college may accept only some of the tests on it, so start with the test your offer letter names. The certificate must be issued within two years of your course start date. Book it close enough to your application that it will still be valid, but early enough to leave time for a resit. If you might later need a UK visa, IELTS Academic is a flexible choice, because its UKVI version has the same format. Nurses should take IELTS Academic or OET in person, because NMBI does not accept at-home versions.

Practising for your test
Our practice tests cover IELTS, TOEFL iBT, PTE Academic, the Duolingo English Test, the Cambridge exams and OET, and the first test of each exam is free. Start with a timed practice test to find your level, then compare your result with the minimum your college or regulator asks for.

English for adults: ESOL and Functional Skills
Adults who are learning English in England often study for ESOL Skills for Life qualifications (Entry 3, Level 1 and Level 2). Adults and apprentices who need an English qualification for work or further study take Functional Skills English at Level 1 or Level 2. Colleges and training providers tell you which level and which awarding body to take.

English tests for the United Kingdom — frequently asked questions

Can I use a normal IELTS test for a UK visa?
No. For a visa that needs a SELT, you must book IELTS for UKVI (or IELTS Life Skills) at an approved centre. The test content is the same as standard IELTS, but the booking and the centre are different.

Is the Duolingo English Test accepted for UK visas?
It is not a SELT, so it cannot be used where the Home Office asks for one. Some universities accept it when they assess your English themselves for a Student visa.

Is TOEFL iBT accepted in the UK?
It is not on the SELT list. Many UK universities still accept it for degree-level admission, because they are allowed to assess your English themselves.

What English level do I need for a Skilled Worker visa?
B2 for new applications made since 8 January 2026. People who already held the visa before that date need B1 when they extend.

How long is a SELT result valid?
The result must have been awarded in the two years before the date you apply.

Is the Duolingo English Test accepted for an Irish study visa?
Yes, it is on the ISD list of recognised tests. Your college may still ask for a specific test or a higher score.

Do I need an English test for an English language course in Ireland?
ISD does not require a test certificate for English language course applicants, but a visa officer may ask for other evidence of basic English.

sources.excerpt: Choosing between the PTE and IELTS test to study or work in the UK? Here’s what you need to know!
sources.text:
PTE or IELTS test for UKVI - which should you take?
Are you planning to study, work and live in the UK? If so, you’ll have to pass your English proficiency test and two popular options come up - the UKVI IELTS and the UKVI PTE.
While both of them are engineered for the UKVI standards, there are significant differences that you must know before making a choice.
In this article, we will go through the differences between UKVI PTE and UKVI IELTS so that you can make an informed decision to reach your goals.

What Is UKVI PTE?
Launched in 2009, the PTE is an English language test that was launched by Pearson Inc. It has two tests: PTE Academic and PTE General, both computer-based and automated.
These tests have only begun to be accepted in recent years by governments like Australia and New Zealand for visa purposes.
PTE-takers will have to sit for the UKVI Academic test for a visa application.

What Is UKVI IELTS?
Set as the golden standard for English proficiency tests, IELTS was launched in 1980 and evaluates the fluency of English in both written and spoken formats.
Accepted by over 13,500 institutions in more than 150 countries, IELTS is the most recognised test of its kind, and the most popular. It has both paper-based and computer-based versions of its test, which is split into four sections: speaking, writing, listening and reading.
If you lean towards reliability and decide to go with IELTS, the suitable test option would be the UKVI IELTS Academic.

Understanding the PTE and IELTS UKVI tests

1. Both tests allow students to study in the UK
If you want to further their studies in the UK, the UKVI Academic version of both the IELTS and PTE are accepted.
Both tests assess the four same skills and are recognised by numerous education institutions based in the UK.

2. Both tests help individuals live and work in the UK
If you are seeking a job as well or looking to live in the UK, you can also take either the IELTS UKVI Life Skills A1 and B1 or PTE UKVI Home A1, A2 and B1.
Approved by the UK home office for visa applications, the UKVI versions of the tests are only available at test centres that meet the administrative requirements outlined by the UK Home Office.
In addition, your test report form will look slightly different than the regular PTE or IELTS tests.

3. IELTS is the preferred qualification vs PTE
As IELTS is the world’s number one English test for migration, it is still favoured over the PTE by most. This is an important distinction o be aware of.
Besides that, PTE is a much newer test as compared to the UKVI IELTS, and is not as recognised globally.
In fact, over 13,500 organisations worldwide trust IELTS’ evaluation of English language skills while only around 3,000 organisations accept the PTE.
If you are looking for the widest breadth of acceptance from a test, IELTS will be the right choice to make. The last thing you want is for your certification to not be recognised, and still ending up needing to take the IELTS test.

4. IELTS offers the option of paper and pen test
If you’re more comfortable with using pen and paper to write your answers, then UKVI IELTS would be a better option.
This is because the PTE is available only on computer, whereas with IELTS you will have the flexibility to choose between taking your test on computer or paper in many locations globally.
Not everyone is comfortable keying in their answers or taking a test on a computer. If that’s you, then IELTS is the way to go.

Take the next step towards studying and working in the UK
Now that you know the differences between the IELTS vs PTE tests, choosing the right one should be a breeze!
If you value widespread recognition of your test, then IELTS is hands down the choice for you.
